definition: Generative models built from invertible transformations, giving exact likelihoods at the cost of architectural constraints.
details: Generative models built from invertible transformations, giving exact likelihoods at the cost of architectural constraints. Historically important, and the conceptual ancestor of flow matching, which relaxed invertibility and now powers state-of-the-art image and speech generation.

explainer.lead: Normalizing flows are generative models built from invertible transformations, giving exact likelihoods at the cost of architectural constraints. They are historically important and the conceptual ancestor of flow matching, which relaxed invertibility and now powers state-of-the-art image and speech generation.

tiers.eli5: It is like a chain of reversible moves that reshapes simple randomness into realistic data, and you can always undo each move to check the math exactly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers stack invertible transformations so likelihoods can be computed exactly. A pitfall is that requiring invertibility constrains the architecture.
tiers.paperLevel: Generative models built from invertible transformations; they give exact likelihoods at the cost of architectural constraints. Flow matching later relaxed invertibility.

explainer.example: A simple base distribution is passed through several invertible layers to model complex data, and the exact likelihood is obtained by tracking the change in density through each layer.
